# World Orogen

> Procedural planet generator — free, browser-based, no signup required.

World Orogen generates realistic procedural planets shaped by tectonic plate simulation, erosion, and climate modeling. It runs entirely in the browser using Three.js and requires no installation, account, or payment.

## What it does

- Generates unique terrestrial planets with realistic continents, mountains, ocean trenches, and volcanic islands
- Simulates tectonic plates with convergent, divergent, and transform boundaries
- Applies glacial, hydraulic, and thermal erosion to carve fjords, river valleys, and talus slopes
- Simulates seasonal climate: wind patterns, ocean currents, precipitation, and Köppen classification
- Creates hotspot volcanism with drift-trail island chains (like Hawaii)
- Allows interactive editing — select multiple tectonic plates for batch reshaping with visual preview before rebuild
- Import your own equirectangular B&W heightmaps (Earth, Mars, hand-drawn) onto a 3D globe with automatic climate simulation
- Evolution: simulates a planet's tectonic history (a supercontinent breaking up, oceans opening and closing, continents colliding) as a timeline to scrub; any moment can be sculpted in detail with rivers, lakes, glaciers, its own climate, a satellite view, a geology view (a rock-type map built from the simulated history — sedimentary basins, volcanic arcs, flood basalts, granite, metamorphic belts, ancient shields — plus its past mountain belts and shallow seas) and a farming view (what the land could grow by rain or with irrigation, its staple crops, the hearths where farming began and how real crops spread from them, how many people it could feed, its soil and growing season), then exported; a planet (its whole history and its detailed moment) saves as one file, to open again later without waiting — the same planet in any browser

## Who it's for

- Worldbuilders creating fantasy or sci-fi settings
- Game developers who need heightmaps for Unity, Unreal, or other engines
- Tabletop RPG players building campaign worlds (D&D, Pathfinder, etc.)
- Fantasy/sci-fi authors designing believable planets
- Artists and hobbyists who enjoy procedural generation
- Educators teaching plate tectonics and planetary science

## Key capabilities

- Multiple views: terrain, satellite biome, Köppen climate, heightmap — on a 3D globe or a flat map in any of ten projections
- Detailed inspection layers for geology, plate physics and climate — the climate ones in real units for the year, January or July: pressure and wind, ocean currents and upwelling, sea ice, temperature, precipitation, temperature range, rain shadow, aridity, growing season, rain seasonality
- Export maps up to 65,536px wide, every map as colour or as 16-bit data on documented scales (heightmaps, hillshade, temperature, rain, pressure, winds, currents, ice, Köppen classes), in ten map projections (equirectangular, Mercator, Robinson, Equal Earth, Mollweide, Hammer, Winkel Tripel, orthographic, azimuthal equidistant, Van der Grinten), one PNG or a ZIP with a README
- Shareable planet codes — copy a compact code to reproduce any planet exactly
- Works on desktop and mobile browsers
- No build step, no dependencies to install — pure ES modules

## Technical details

- Built with Three.js (WebGL), vanilla JavaScript ES modules
- Fibonacci sphere meshing with Voronoi tessellation
- Braun-Willett stream power erosion, Barnes et al. pit-filling algorithm
- Coupled climate on a fixed 1° grid: seasonal energy balance, derived pressure belts and winds, wind-driven ocean gyres with upwelling (seasonal in the tropics), and a column-water rain budget — a few seconds at any resolution; Köppen from each region's twelve months
- Fully client-side — no server, no data collection
